title: Specified Skilled Worker food manufacturing will split into two job categories in April 2027
summary: Japan's Immigration Services Agency says the Specified Skilled Worker food-and-beverage manufacturing category will be divided into “food manufacturing” and “seafood processing” from April 1, 2027. The agency also updated SSW field guidance and intake/resident data in late August and on September 4.
why_it_matters: Foreign workers and employers using the SSW system may need to check which job description and field rules apply to future applications, renewals or job changes, especially in seafood-processing work.

claims.text: On September 4, 2026, the Immigration Services Agency updated its information on projected intake and resident numbers for Specified Skilled Worker Type 1 by field.
The SSW food-and-beverage manufacturing work category is scheduled to split into “food manufacturing” and “seafood processing” from April 1, 2027.
ISA amended field-specific guidance for building cleaning, railway and food-and-beverage manufacturing on August 28, 2026.

Workers and employers whose duties include seafood processing should verify the post-April-2027 job classification before a future application, renewal or job change rather than assuming today's field label will remain sufficient.
claims.basis: Announced field split and recent guidance amendments

whats_new: The agency refreshed SSW intake/resident information on September 4.
Food-and-beverage manufacturing field guidance was amended on August 28.
From April 1, 2027, the current broad work category separates food manufacturing from seafood processing.
content.recommendation: If your SSW work touches seafood processing, keep your job description and employer documents clear and re-check ISA's field guidance before any application or renewal approaching April 2027.
content.skeptical_view: This is not a blanket cancellation of existing SSW status. The practical effect depends on the worker's actual duties and the detailed transition/application rules.
content.what_next: Watch for ISA transition guidance, document lists and field-specific application instructions before April 2027.
content.what_would_change_mind: ALAM should revise this if ISA changes the April 1, 2027 split date, scope, transition treatment or required documentation.

30 sec: Japan is changing one SSW work category from April 1, 2027.
Food manufacturing and seafood processing will become separate categories.
Workers and employers should verify the correct field before future applications or renewals.
reading_levels.2_min: Japan's Immigration Services Agency has continued updating the Specified Skilled Worker system. Its food-and-beverage manufacturing page now states that the current broad work category will be split into food manufacturing and seafood processing from April 1, 2027. This matters most for workers and employers whose actual duties involve seafood processing. The announcement does not by itself mean current residence status is invalid; the safe move is to verify the correct classification and later transition guidance before an application, renewal or job change.
